Appreciate the clear ask and the deadline. We can definitely put draft language in front of your legal team. Initial approach: two pragmatic paths so procurement can choose quickly:

Option A — Hosted SLA (standard):
- Uptime: 99.95% monthly availability for hosted endpoints; credits start at <99.95%.
- Latency: regional guidance only (non-contractual) unless Dedicated is procured.

Option B — Dedicated SLA (recommended for your use case):
- Dedicated/GPU-reserved pool with regional placement (us-west).
- Contractual P99 latency target: baseline proposal P99 <= 200ms for avg seq len 512 tokens for our recommended model families.
- Credit schedule: scaled credits starting at 99.9%, with defined remediation windows.
- Exception carve-outs: planned maintenance (48h notice), KV-cache warm-up (up to 10 minutes after model swap), force majeure.

I'll attach a short draft appendix (word) you can share with legal. If you prefer, we can embed the SLO table directly in the order form rather than a standalone addendum.

Olga / Marissa —

High-level feasibility notes from runtime: we can meet HelixCare's request under Dedicated with the following constraints and mitigations:

- Baseline: for typical text-gen workloads (seq len ~512) with quantized model variants and pinned GPU capacity, we see P99 in the 150-220ms range depending on batching and exact model family. 180-200ms is feasible on a well-sized Dedicated pool with carry capacity for burst headroom.

- Recommendations for contract language:
  * Define the P99 measurement window (per calendar month, 1-minute sliding windows aggregated to month).
  * Specify the canonical sequence length and model family or provide a table per-model (we can reference the attached performance_matrix.csv).
  * Allow a transparent warm-up exception: up to 10 minutes after a model swap or topology change where KV cache is rehydrating; this event must be tagged in our Console and visible to the customer (metric: cache_hit_ratio and a warm-up boolean).
  * Include a fallback policy: if P99 breach persists >72 hours, automatic fallback to a capacity-scaling plan or temporary routing to a compatible model variant (customer consent required for model variant fallback).

- Credits: engineering doesn't drive credits but we can emit measurement artifacts (monthly P99 reports, per-request traces) to support third-party audits. We should keep credit thresholds simple and tied to the measurement window above.

I attached a small performance matrix that maps model families to expected P99 bands under Dedicated at different pool sizes. If legal wants strict contractual P99, we should pin model family and commit sizing in the order form. Otherwise we propose a P99 envelope with a per-model table as an exhibit.

Happy to jump on a quick 20m call with HelixCare if helpful.

Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
